clue.text: Nasty head, as it were, seen round middle of wen

indicators.note: something seen round another surrounds it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a hatful is as much as fills a hat, loosely a head's worth, hence 'as it were'

indicators.note: picks the central letter of the word wen

explanation.surface: Someone with a nasty head wound, a wen being a cyst, rather than a nice head.
explanation.walkthrough: HATFUL (Chambers: as much as will fill a hat) is stretched to 'head' with 'as it were'; the E from the middle of 'wen' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hateful and nasty are close synonyms for something odious or very unpleasant.

clue.text: Oral affliction? His is a lot, unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events disorders things, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sympathising that a man has more than his share of a mouth complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Halitosis is bad breath, a complaint of the mouth.

clue.text: Test route requiring turn in main road?

indicators.note: the letters of the road are turned round inside the route word

parts.note: a trail is a path or route
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A driving test route with a turning on to a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; 'requiring turn in' flips its letters within the route word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test of performance or quality.

clue.text: Particularly marks way of speaking? It's something found on the street

parts.note: to flag something is to mark it out for particular attention
tone is the manner or pitch of the voice

explanation.surface: Musing on the marks particular to an accent, found on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is a flat paving slab, part of a pavement.

clue.text: Insect delineated path leading to top of trench

parts.note: in geometry a locus is the path traced by a moving point

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: A bug marching along a marked track to the lip of a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a large grasshopper that swarms and destroys crops.

clue.text: Images enthralling a singular old artist

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the first piece holds the next ones inside it

parts.note: pics is informal for pictures or images
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Some pictures captivate us with a unique painter of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular old' reads as describing the artist, but each word just gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter, is an example of an artist.

clue.text: A warning cry linked to golf target? It offers some protection

parts.note: the pin is the flagstick on a golf green
fore is the golfer's shouted warning

explanation.surface: A golfer's shout near the flag, offering a little safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives A FORE then PIN; 'linked to' lets them join in either order.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or overdress worn to protect clothes.

clue.text: Credit frequently supplying Scottish farm

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
oft is a poetic word for often

explanation.surface: Regular loans keep a Highland smallholding going.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Collection of rubbish? Difficulty, apparently, about height

indicators.note: the earlier pieces go round the next letter

parts.note: a scrape is an awkward predicament
AP is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently

explanation.surface: A query whether a heap of junk is a real height problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' is not a comment on the difficulty but its dictionary abbreviation; 'about' wraps the height letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded junk or waste material.

clue.text: Vast amount Italian writer picked up with article

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A huge amount of Italian literature was collected along with an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceans, informally, means a huge amount, as in oceans of time.

clue.text: Early Russian space traveller crashed in Baikal, losing head

indicators.note: a craft that crashes is wrecked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word Baikal drops its first letter, its head

explanation.surface: A Soviet spacecraft came down in Lake Baikal and its pilot was decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes B off BAIKAL, leaving AIKAL, which 'crashed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Laika was the dog sent into orbit aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957, the first animal to orbit Earth.

clue.text: Area to study supplied by syllabus

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a course of study follows a syllabus

explanation.surface: A student is given a field of study by the course outline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area' looks like a subject area; it is an open space, as in a station's concourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large open space or hall where people gather, as in a station.

clue.text: Cheers stories, but not Independent stories

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

indicators.note: says the following letter is left out of the preceding word

parts.note: lies are stories in the sense of fibs

explanation.surface: A pub toast to anecdotes, excluding those from this very newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' winks at the newspaper printing the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are narratives or yarns told for entertainment.

clue.text: What could fasten edges of frilly panties, loose?

indicators.note: loose letters are not held in order, so they are rearranged
takes the first and last letters of the word frilly

explanation.surface: A question about how to secure underwear that has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges of' gives FY, and 'loose' rearranges FY plus PANTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is a bent pin with a clasp, used to hold cloth together.

clue.text: Society indifferent about hospital training establishment

indicators.note: one word is placed around another letter

parts.note: cool means unenthusiastic or indifferent
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An apathetic society running a hospital's nurse-training college.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is an institution where people are taught or trained.

clue.text: What makes that man beam about end of scheme — future possibilities?

parts.note: he refers to that man

indicators.note: the beam word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping roof beam

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word scheme

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what makes a man smile at the end of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like smiling but is a roof timber; 'about' places E within RAFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereafter is the future, especially life after death.

clue.text: Journalists getting around including member of royal family

indicators.note: the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: the press is the collective term for journalists
INC is the abbreviation for including (inclusive)

explanation.surface: Reporters swarming round, a royal among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' reads as a link but supplies its own abbreviation; 'getting around' wraps the journalists round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a daughter or female relative of a monarch.

clue.text: Location of writing? No record when consumed by candle

indicators.note: the record is swallowed, so it goes inside the candle

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: No trace of the document after it was burned by a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepaper is stationery on which letters are written.

clue.text: Lumpy son, unfortunate, requiring injection of energy

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the letter enters the word

parts.note: hapless means unlucky or unfortunate
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ill-formed, unlucky son needing a shot of vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpy and shapeless both describe something lacking a definite form.

clue.text: Elevated purpose in Volume 5 is engaging Unionist, a source of hot stuff

indicators.note: the raised word sits between the two letters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read upwards

parts.note: use means purpose, as in what's the use

indicators.note: to engage is to hold, so the word goes round the next letter

explanation.surface: A book volume describing a Unionist as a hothead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' works because this is a down clue: the purpose word reads upwards. '5' is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesuvius is the volcano near Naples, a source of lava.

clue.text: Master of dark arts more unhappy about church, right?

indicators.note: the first word surrounds the next letters

parts.note: sorer means more aggrieved or upset
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A warlock grows more discontented with the church, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer is a wizard who practises black magic.

clue.text: More work? Extremely urgent work I advanced

indicators.note: takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the word urgent

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Asking for more work, then an urgent assignment pushes forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, the Tudor statesman, not 'additional'; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia (1516) is Thomas More's book describing an ideal island state.

clue.text: London guards desire securing house in part of East London

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

parts.words: house in part of East London
parts.note: Cockneys drop their h's, so home becomes 'ome

explanation.surface: The Tower's guards long to keep a house in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech of London's East End drops initial H, turning HOME into 'OME.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard (Beefeaters) guard the Tower of London.

clue.text: £1000 outstanding? King's called in nobleman

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

indicators.note: one letter is brought inside another word

parts.note: an outstanding bill is due
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A grand still owed, so the king has summoned an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's' is King has: K is called into DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand duke is a high-ranking noble, often ruling a grand duchy.

clue.text: Collection of people climb, carrying rope to start with

indicators.note: the climbing phrase carries the next letter inside it

parts.note: to go up is to climb

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word rope

explanation.surface: A climbing team going up with a rope at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a number of people gathered or classed together.

clue.text: Plan about river is not sound

indicators.note: the second word wraps around the river letter

parts.note: daft means silly, not of sound mind

explanation.surface: A scheme concerning a river is ill-conceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' but puts DAFT around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline plan.

clue.text: Investigator actually overlooking it, causing annoyance

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: overlooking something misses it out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: quite, said as agreement, means just so, actually

explanation.surface: A detective really ignoring a clue, to everyone's irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is resentment or irritation from wounded pride.

clue.text: Question computer experts over South American city

parts.note: IT, information technology, stands for computer people
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Quizzing IT specialists about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital of Ecuador.

clue.text: Form of ban omits cars when on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A traffic ban that excludes cars while they are moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism is exclusion from a group, a social ban; originally banishment in ancient Athens.

clue.text: Description of some numbers in formal basis of logarithms

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A maths textbook describing numbers in the strict foundations of logarithms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basis' here is the mathematical base: natural logarithms use the constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime number has no divisors but itself and one, so prime describes some numbers.

clue.text: Buccaneers arranged a disturbed stretch of water on return

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: set means arranged or put in place
a rip is a stretch of water made rough by meeting currents

explanation.surface: Pirates lining up turbulent seas for their voyage home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns SET A RIP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Buccaneers were pirates who raided Spanish ships in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Uneasy over playing in hot weather, on reflection

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the reversed word
a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word is reversed

parts.note: sun stands for sunny hot weather

indicators.note: letters at play move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anxious about performing outdoors in a heatwave, thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges OVER into ERVO, and 'on reflection' turns SUN into NUS; ERVO goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means anxious or apprehensive, close to uneasy.
